status.nb: 121 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen attacked a Plateau community, killing 16 and injuring four, while suspected militants killed at least 30 people in Niger state. Bandits abducted six people in Kaduna and six in Chikun LGA, and gunmen opened fire on Peter Obi supporters in Edo, injuring one person. President Tinubu pledged to rescue abducted schoolchildren in Borno and to intensify operations against terrorists, while law enforcement officials reaffirmed a refusal to negotiate with bandits. Amnesty International condemned the Tinubu government for inaction after a mass burial of Plateau victims. 1,486 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn angrep et samfunn i Plateau, drepte 16 og såret fire, mens mistenkte militante drepte minst 30 personer i Niger delstat. Banditter bortførte seks personer i Kaduna og seks i Chikun LGA, og væpnede menn skjøt mot støttespillere til Peter Obi i Edo, og såret én person. President Tinubu lovet å redde bortførte skolebarn i Borno og å intensivere operasjoner mot terrorister, mens rettshåndhevende myndigheter gjentok at de ikke vil forhandle med banditter. Amnesty International fordømte Tinubu-regjeringen for inaktivitet etter en massebegraving av ofrene i Plateau. 1,486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
